reason: The cited evidence does not directly support the key premises. E2 and E3 show Ti-rich intermetallics/oxides can improve corrosion resistance in Mg alloys, but none of the passages address laser remelting of MgAlCuZnGd, formation of a supersaturated metastable layer, its transformation into a protective intermetallic/oxide network, or its effect on oxidation kinetics. The evidence is only loosely related to the proposed mechanism.
premises: Laser remelting can produce a uniform supersaturated metastable surface layer on MgAlCuZnGd
High-temperature oxidation transforms this metastable layer into a finely dispersed intermetallic/oxide network
This intermetallic/oxide network acts as a diffusion barrier, reducing oxygen and corrosive species ingress
The transformed surface layer leads to lower oxidation rate and enhanced corrosion resistance vs. as-cast
Ti-rich intermetallics or oxides can act as corrosion barriers in Mg-containing alloys
